chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of rs11629191 in breast cancer
predictions: No allele-specific TF binding at rs11629191 is detectable in MCF7 chromatin.
No allelic difference is seen in reporter assays in MCF7.
No breast-tissue eQTL for PELI2 or ENSG00000259868 is attributable to this variant.
PELI2 perturbation has no breast-cancer-relevant growth phenotype, consistent with DepMap non-dependency.
falsified_if: Allele-specific TF binding at rs11629191 is demonstrated in MCF7 cells.
A reproducible allelic effect on a target gene or reporter is shown in a breast-cell context.
ChIP, CUT&RUN, or reporter assays contradict the no-effect prediction.

chains.title: XBP1 binds the ref C allele more strongly at a candidate non-cCRE motif

links.claim: XBP1 is the strongest QBiC-SELEX group member: group G382 reports XBP1 own model with z=-91.69 and effect=-3.167, meaning the alt T allele binds less than ref C, and XBP1 is expressed at 636.57 TPM in the MCF7 context. E18 reports no ENCODE XBP1 ChIP-seq peak containing the variant in MCF7, but absence can also mean no XBP1 experiment in that biosample, so cellular occupancy is unproven.

The variant is an intronic/intergenic variant with no overlapping ENCODE cCRE; the nearest cCRE is 1,868 bp away. This is at most a candidate XBP1 motif outside a chromatin-defined regulatory element.

PELI2 is the nearest protein-coding gene but lies 230.8 kb upstream, and no provided evidence directly links rs11629191 or XBP1 to PELI2. E19 reports no significant GTEx v8 breast eQTL for this variant, E05 contains only a PIP 0.03 brain-nucleus-accumbens eQTL for ENSG00000259868, and E20 shows PELI2 is not a common-essential gene in breast lines.
XBP1 is expressed at 636.57 TPM in DepMap ACH-000019 (MCF7), so XBP1 is present at high levels in the relevant cell context.

No provided evidence connects XBP1 at this locus to breast cancer: E04 shows zero GWAS Catalog associations for rs11629191, E06 is only a PELI2 keyword-hit list without a demonstrated XBP1-rs11629191-PELI2 axis, and E20 shows PELI2 non-dependency in breast lines. The phenotype link remains speculative.

predictions: XBP1 ChIP-qPCR or CUT&RUN in MCF7 shows occupancy at rs11629191.
The ref C allele has higher XBP1 occupancy than the alt T allele.

XBP1 perturbation changes PELI2 expression only if PELI2 is the long-range target.

chains.title: CREB3L4 binds the ref C allele more strongly at a candidate bZIP motif

links.claim: The G017 CREB3-family bZIP group binds the ref C allele more strongly than the alt T allele: best model CREB3 has z=-76.89 and effect=-1.64 (alt binds less), and CREB3L4 is an own-model member with the same direction (z=-37.55). CREB3L4 is chosen because it is the highest-expressed member in MCF7 at 48.8 TPM, but this remains in vitro SELEX without cellular occupancy data.

The variant is intronic/intergenic and does not overlap an ENCODE cCRE; the nearest cCRE is 1,868 bp away. The element claim is therefore a candidate CREB3-family motif, not a validated regulatory element.

The only molecular QTL in the credible set is a PIP 0.03 eQTL for ENSG00000259868 in brain nucleus accumbens, which is very weak and in a non-breast tissue. E19 reports no significant breast GTEx eQTL for this variant, so no breast variant-to-gene link is established.
CREB3L4 is expressed at 48.8 TPM in DepMap ACH-000019 (MCF7), making it a plausibly expressed member of the G017 group in this cell context.

No provided evidence directly connects CREB3L4 at rs11629191 to breast cancer; E04 shows zero GWAS Catalog associations for the variant. Breast cancer relevance is inferred only from the case context.

grades_v0.reason: QBiC-SELEX group G382 gives XBP1 own model z=-91.69, effect=-3.167 (alt binds less), directionally consistent with allele_binding_more=ref, and XBP1 is 636.57 TPM in MCF7. But this is in vitro SELEX only: there is no ChIP/CUT&RUN, MPRA or allele-specific assay, and the best model's site strength is ref 100.0th vs alt 98.7th percentile, a modest model-level difference. Per instructions, a SELEX binding change alone is at best weak.

E01 reports intron_variant with no regulatory features and E03 states no cCRE overlaps the variant, nearest EH38E1716463 (dELS) 1,868 bp away. The claim that this is at most a candidate motif outside a chromatin-defined element is exactly what the evidence shows.

E02 supports only that PELI2 is the nearest protein-coding TSS (230.8 kb upstream). No QTL, chromatin-loop or perturbation evidence links rs11629191 or XBP1 to PELI2. E06 is a keyword-hit list (178 hits) whose top titles do not report PELI2 breast-cancer mechanism, so it supports plausibility at most. A 230 kb nearest-gene assignment is not a target-gene link.
E08 reports XBP1 at 636.57 TPM in the DepMap/ACH-000019 (MCF7) expression context used by the screen, which directly supports that XBP1 is highly expressed in this cell type.

No cited evidence connects XBP1 at this locus to breast cancer. E06 is a generic PELI2 keyword search whose listed PMIDs concern other topics (Pellino review, thyroid parthanatos, tramadol, BRCA1/pemetrexed, etc.); none reports an XBP1-rs11629191-PELI2-breast cancer axis. E04 shows 0 GWAS Catalog associations for the variant.

G017's best model is CREB3 (z=-76.89, effect=-1.64, alt binds less); CREB3L4 is an own-model member with the same sign (z=-37.55) and is the highest-expressed member (48.8 TPM). Choosing CREB3L4 rather than the best model CREB3 is given a stated reason (expression), which is acceptable, and direction is consistent. However this remains in vitro SELEX with no cellular binding data, and the best model's site strength is only ref 99.9th vs alt 98.2nd percentile.
E01 (intron_variant, no regulatory features) and E03 (no overlapping cCRE, nearest 1,868 bp) directly support that this is a candidate motif in a non-cCRE element, as claimed.

The only cited molecular link is E05: an eQTL for ENSG00000259868 with PIP 0.03 in GTEx brain nucleus accumbens. PIP 0.03 is essentially null and the tissue is not breast, so the claim that this is a 'very weak and non-breast QTL link' is accurate, but it does not establish a variant-to-gene effect; E02 gives no distance for ENSG00000259868.
E09 gives CREB3L4 at 48.8 TPM in the DepMap ACH-000019 (MCF7) context, directly supporting expression of this group member in the case's cell type.
No evidence IDs are cited and none of the provided evidence links CREB3L4 at rs11629191 to breast cancer. The chain itself concedes the link is inferred purely from the case context.

G033 gives ATF2 own model z=-49.19, effect=-1.348 (alt binds less), directionally consistent with allele_binding_more=ref; ATF2 is 16.22 TPM in MCF7. But the TF-selection rationale is weak: ATF7 is in the same group with its own model and is more highly expressed (20.81 TPM vs 16.22 TPM), so 'ATF2 is expressed' does not distinguish it from ATF7. And the binding evidence is in vitro SELEX only, with modest site-strength shift (ref 99.7th vs alt 95.7th percentile).
E01 (intron_variant, no regulatory features) and E03 (no cCRE within 500 bp; nearest cCRE 1,868 bp) support the claim that the only element evidence is an in vitro motif disruption, not a cCRE.

Only E02 nearest-gene distance (PELI2, 230.8 kb upstream) plus E06 keyword literature support this; there is no ATF2-PELI2 or variant-PELI2 QTL/perturbation evidence, and the E06 titles do not demonstrate PELI2 breast-cancer mechanism.
E11 reports ATF2 at 16.22 TPM in the MCF7 expression context, which is exactly what the link claims (expression only).
No evidence connects ATF2 at rs11629191 to breast cancer; E06 only supports broad PELI2 keyword plausibility, and E04 shows no GWAS association for the variant.

E12 shows the G064 CxxC group with best model CXXC4 (z=-44.11, effect=-2.102, alt binds less) and CXXC5 listed as mapped (77.02 TPM), so the chain correctly discloses that the CXXC5 direction is inferred from related CxxC models rather than a CXXC5 own model. That is indirect (mapped coverage) and in vitro; the best model's site-strength shift is large (ref 98.8th vs alt 70.2nd percentile), but CXXC4 itself is only 0.33 TPM in MCF7, so the passing members and the expressed members are different factors.
E01 (intron_variant, no regulatory features) and E03 (no cCRE overlap, nearest 1,868 bp) directly support the claim that this is a candidate motif rather than a validated regulatory element.

E05's ENSG00000259868 eQTL has PIP 0.03 in brain nucleus accumbens: it is consistent with a 'weak' link, but PIP 0.03 is effectively no credible set signal and the tissue is wrong for the breast cancer context; no perturbation evidence is cited for this gene.
E12 reports CXXC5 at 77.02 TPM in MCF7, so the claim that CXXC5 is the most plausible expressed CxxC-group member is supported, with the caveat (already stated) that its coverage is mapped-only.
No evidence IDs are cited, and nothing in E01-E17 connects CXXC5 at rs11629191 to breast cancer; E04 gives 0 GWAS Catalog associations for the variant.

ATF2 is the best model in G033, but ATF7 is also an own-model member and slightly more highly expressed, so the TF choice is not strongly distinguished. checks.why: All four chains' binding links rest on QBiC-SELEX in vitro predictions with no cellular occupancy evidence. A Factorbook/ENCODE ChIP-seq lookup for XBP1 in MCF7 would either firmly falsify the strongest chain (XBP1, highest expression, largest z) or upgrade it from weak to supported; the same logic applies to the other group-based TF picks.

The only molecular QTL in E05 is a PIP 0.03 eQTL in brain nucleus accumbens, which is effectively null and in the wrong tissue. A breast-tissue GTEx eQTL lookup would either supply a credible variant-to-gene link for ENSG00000259868/PELI2 (rescuing the 'gene' links of the CREB3L4 and CXXC5 chains) or confirm that no gene link exists at all.

The phenotype links of the XBP1 and ATF2 chains both end at PELI2 on the basis of the E06 keyword list, which contains no PELI2 mechanistic paper. A DepMap knockout lookup for PELI2 in breast-lineage lines tests whether perturbing the proposed target gene even has a cancer-relevant phenotype, which is the largest remaining gap above 'weak' for two chains.
